text:
Jia Chen: Heads up — noticed a tail-latency spike hitting YVR POP around 2026-03-18T15:20Z. p95/p99 for gen requests (short seq <= 16) jumped ~3-4x. Affects model: redwood-open-7b-q4 and 13b-q4. Thought it might be noisy tenant but load didn't change.

perf-bot: alert: yvr-pop-high-tail-latency triggered (p99>120ms) at 2026-03-18T15:21:10Z

Matt R.: quick capture: kernel selector logs show rapid fallback to generic_matmul_atn_fallback and batch sizes collapsed to 1 for a 90s window.
```
[15:20:41] kernel_selector: seq_len=8 chosen=generic_matmul_atn_fallback latency_est=4.8ms
[15:20:42] batching: active_batch_size=1 window_ms=6 reason=low_coalescence
[15:21:05] kv_cache: miss_rate=0.54 evictions=1200/s
```

Sofia P.: prometheus snippet — kv cache working set looked stable but miss_rate spiked with a correlated increase in rpc RTT variance.
```
avg(rpc_round_trip_ms{pop="yvr"}[2m]) = 3.1 -> 9.6
histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) = 110ms -> 420ms
```

Ryan K.: traceroute to backend at spike start shows path change via ASN 12345 -> ASN 67890, intermediate hop shows +2-4ms jitter. Suspect provider microbursts at peering.

Matt R.: hypothesis: kernel selection heuristic treats sudden RTT increase as host slowness -> switches to fallback kernel with worse throughput but lower p99 under packet-loss scenarios; combined with batching heuristic that shrinks window when inter-arrival appears low -> we degenerate to singleton batches + more KV churn.

Jia Chen: agree. Quick rollback plan: pin kernel selector to prefer high-throughput kernel for seq_len<=16 and force minimum batching window 12ms on YVR pool; ops to apply now.

ops-bot: deploy started by @Matt R. — feature-flag: yvr.kernel_force_pref=high_throughput, yvr.batch_min_window_ms=12

Matt R.: patch applied, observing batch sizes climb back to 6-8 and p99 recovering toward baseline over last 30s.

Sofia P.: KV miss rate and evictions falling. RTT variance still noisy but impact mitigated.

Jia Chen: Root cause (so far): transient peering microbursts caused short-lived RTT spikes; our kernel selection and batching heuristics interpreted that as host-level slowdown and moved to conservative execution path causing throughput collapse. Action items:
- Perf team: make kernel selector smoother (median over 50 samples) and add hysteresis before switching to fallback
- Runtime: ensure batching min_window_ms default isn't reactive to single-sample gaps
- Networking: open ticket with provider (ASN 67890) and attach traceroutes
- Postmortem if not closed in 24h

Ryan K.: filing provider ticket now — ticket 78942 created.

Jia Chen: thanks all — continue to monitor. :white_check_mark:
